spots.name: Coventry Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of Saint Michael, commonly known as Coventry Cathedral, is the seat of the Bishop of Coventry and the Diocese of Coventry within the Church of England. The cathedral is located in Coventry, West Midlands, England.

spots.name: University of Warwick
spots.summary: The University of Warwick is a public research university on the outskirts of Coventry between the West Midlands and Warwickshire, England. The university was founded in 1965 as part of a government initiative to expand higher education.

spots.name: Coventry Transport Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Coventry Transport Museum is a transport museum, located in Coventry city centre, England.

spots.name: Herbert Art Gallery and Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Herbert Art Gallery & Museum is a museum, art gallery, records archive, learning centre, media studio and creative arts facility on Jordan Well, Coventry, England.

names.ja: ハーバート美術博物館

spots.name: Coventry railway station
spots.summary: Coventry railway station serves the city of Coventry, in the West Midlands, England. It lies on the Birmingham loop of the West Coast Main Line (WCML); it is also located at the centre of a junction where the lines to Nuneaton and to Leamington converge.

spots.name: St Michael's Victory over the Devil
spots.summary: St Michael's Victory over the Devil is a 1958 bronze sculpture by Jacob Epstein, displayed on the south end of the east wall outside of the new Coventry Cathedral, above the steps leading up from Priory Street to the cathedral's entrance and beside the stained glass of John Piper's bowed baptistry window.

spots.name: Holy Trinity Church, Coventry

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Holy Trinity Church, Coventry, is a parish church of the Church of England in Coventry, West Midlands, England. Above the chancel arch is an impressive doom wall-painting.

spots.name: St Mary's Priory and Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Mary's Priory and Cathedral was an institution in Coventry, England, founded in the 12th century by transformation of the former monastery of St Mary, and destroyed during the Dissolution of the Monasteries in the early 16th century.

names.fr: Prieuré et cathédrale de Sainte-Marie de Coventry
names.es: Priorato y catedral de Santa María

spots.name: Coventry Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Coventry Castle was a motte and bailey castle in the city of Coventry, England. It was demolished in the late 12th century and St Mary's Guildhall was built on part of the site.

spots.name: Self Sacrifice
spots.summary: Self Sacrifice, better known as the Lady Godiva statue is an equestrian statue of Lady Godiva in Broadgate, Coventry. The statue is bronze, on a plinth of Portland stone.

spots.name: Coombe Abbey
spots.summary: Coombe Abbey is a former Cistercian abbey at Combe Fields in the Borough of Rugby, in the countryside of Warwickshire, England. The abbey was converted to a country house in the 16th century and now operates as a hotel. It is a grade I listed building.

spots.name: St Mary's Guildhall

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: St Mary's Hall is a municipal building in Bayley Lane in Coventry, West Midlands, England. It is a Grade I listed building.

spots.name: Midland Air Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Midland Air Museum (MAM) is situated just outside the village of Baginton in Warwickshire, England, and is adjacent to Coventry Airport. The museum includes the Sir Frank Whittle Jet Heritage Centre, where many exhibits are on display in a large hangar.

names.ja: ミッドランド航空博物館

spots.name: Whittle Arch
spots.summary: The Whittle Arch is a public art installation in Coventry, England. It is dedicated to Sir Frank Whittle, the inventor of the turbojet engine, who was born in Coventry. The arch was designed as part of Coventry's Phoenix Initiative regeneration project at the start of the 21st century.

spots.name: Coventry city walls
spots.summary: Coventry's city walls are a sequence of defensive structures built around the city of Coventry in England.

spots.name: Belgrade Theatre
spots.summary: The Belgrade Theatre is a live performance venue in Coventry, England. It was the first civic theatre to be built in Britain after the Second World War and is now a Grade II listed building.

spots.name: Council House, Coventry
spots.summary: The Council House, Coventry in Coventry, England, is a Tudor Revival style city hall building which is the home of Coventry City Council and the seat of local government. It was built in the early 20th century. It is a Grade II-listed building.

spots.name: Coventry Cross
spots.summary: Coventry Cross was an important landmark in the cathedral city of Coventry, England. Standing between Cuckoo Lane and Holy Trinity Church and in the alley known as Trinity Churchyard, it was a modern version of the historic market cross, such as was common in many medieval market towns.

spots.name: Spon Street
spots.summary: Spon Street is an historic street in central Coventry, in the West Midlands of England. The street was once part of a route that ran from Gosford to Birmingham – a route which remained intact until the 1960s.

spots.name: The Wave, Coventry
spots.summary: The Wave is an indoor waterpark situated in Coventry in the West Midlands, England. The waterpark currently holds the record for the largest wave pool in the UK, at a capacity of 20 million litres.

spots.name: Golden Cross
spots.summary: The Golden Cross is one of the oldest pubs in Coventry, West Midlands, and one of the longest-established alcohol-serving venues in England.

photo.author: The Nicholson Family (Wikipedia Takes Coventry participant)

spots.name: Coventry Building Society Arena
spots.summary: The Coventry Building Society Arena is a complex in Coventry, West Midlands, England. It includes a 32,609-seater stadium which is currently home to Premier League club Coventry City, along with facilities which include a 6,000 square metre exhibition hall, a hotel and a casino.

spots.name: Lady Herbert's Garden
spots.summary: Lady Herbert's Garden is a garden in Coventry city centre, named as a memorial to Alfred Herbert's second wife Florence. Construction and initial laying out began in 1930 and the last section was completed in 1939.

spots.name: Cook Street Gate
spots.summary: Cook Street Gate is a medieval gate in Coventry, England. It was probably built in the second half of the 14th century as part of the defensive circuit of the city.

spots.name: Electric Railway Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Electric Railway Museum was located near to the village of Baginton, south-east of Coventry, in Warwickshire, England. The heritage railway centre was immediately adjacent to Coventry Airport and so it was also known as "The Airfield Line"; the site was leased from Coventry City Council.

names.ja: 電気鉄道博物館 (ウォリックシャー)

spots.name: Old Grammar School, Coventry

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Old Grammar School, Coventry is a Grade I listed building in Coventry, England on the corner of Bishop Street and Hales Street.

spots.name: All Saints Church, Allesley

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: All Saints Church is a mediaeval church in the suburban village of Allesley adjoining the City of Coventry, in the West Midlands of England. The building is grade I listed, though churches in ecclesiastical use are exempt from listed building procedures.

spots.name: St John the Baptist Church, Coventry

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Collegiate and Parish Church of St John the Baptist is an English church located in the Medieval area of Spon Street in the city centre of Coventry, West Midlands. The church is a Grade I listed building.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St John the Baptist Church, Coventry

spots.name: Greyfriars, Coventry

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Greyfriars was a medieval Franciscan priory in Coventry, England. The original monastic buildings were lost in the English Reformation; the spire standing on the site today was most recently part of a 19th-century church that was destroyed in an air raid in the Second World War.

spots.name: Drapers' Hall
spots.summary: Drapers' Hall is a historic building in the Cathedral Quarter of Coventry built in 1832 by the Drapers' Company, a large trading guild in Coventry. The present building is believed to the third guildhall on the site.

spots.name: The Charterhouse

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Charterhouse, Coventry is a grade I listed building on London Road, Coventry, in the West Midlands, England.

photo.author: Carmen McLean-Ellmann, Oliver Ellmann (Wikipedia Takes Coventry participant)

spots.name: Coventry ring road
spots.summary: The Coventry ring road, designated as the A4053, is a 2.25-mile (3.62 km) ring road in Coventry, England, which forms a complete dual-carriageway loop around the city centre. The road encompasses the old and new Coventry Cathedrals, the city's shopping areas and much of Coventry University.

spots.name: London Road Cemetery
spots.summary: London Road Cemetery is a 17-hectare (42-acre) cemetery in Coventry, England, designed by Joseph Paxton and opened in 1847.

spots.name: The Old Windmill
spots.summary: The Old Windmill is a public house in Spon Street in Coventry, England. It is a Grade II Listed, 15th-century building with a history going back to around 1451 when it constructed around the trunk of a tree.

spots.name: War Memorial Park
spots.summary: The War Memorial Park is a large park of about 48.5 hectares in southern Coventry, England. The park was opened in July 1921 as a tribute to the 2,587 Coventrians who died between 1914 and 1918 fighting in the First World War.

spots.name: County Hall, Coventry
spots.summary: County Hall is a historic former courthouse in Cuckoo Lane in Coventry's Cathedral Quarter. It is a Grade II* listed building.

spots.name: Gosford Street
spots.summary: Gosford Street is one of Coventry's most historic streets, located on the edge of the city centre, just beyond the inner ring road. Far Gosford Street is one of the few streets in Coventry that survived modernization, dilapidation and the Blitz.

spots.name: 38–39 Bayley Lane
spots.summary: 38–39 Bayley Lane is a former building, whose present-day site is accessible from the Herbert Art Gallery and Museum in Coventry, England. All that remains is the medieval undercroft, a fourteenth-century cellar that initially belonged to a wealthy merchant, who was a clothier.

spots.name: Coventry War Memorial
spots.summary: Coventry War Memorial stands at the centre of War Memorial Park, to the south of the city of Coventry in England. The memorial is a tapering tower 87 feet (27 m) high, completed in 1927. It was restored in 2011, and designated as a Grade II* listed building in January 2013.

spots.name: Stone House, Allesley
spots.summary: Stone House is a 16th-century sandstone house on Birmingham Road in Allesley, Coventry. It is Grade II* listed for a number of architectural features, as well as its good condition.

spots.name: Bond's Hospital
spots.summary: Bond's Hospital is an almshouse in Coventry, England, established for old bedesmen. It is a Grade II* listed building.

spots.name: Caludon Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Caludon Castle is a Scheduled Ancient Monument and Grade I listed building in Coventry, in the West Midlands of England. A second moated site 190 metres (620 ft) to the south is a Scheduled Ancient Monument in its own right. The castle is now a ruin, and all that remains is a large fragment of sandstone wall.

spots.name: Lunt Roman Fort

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Lunt Roman fort is the archaeological site of a Roman fort, of unknown name, in the Roman province of Britannia. It is open to the public and located in the village of Baginton on the south eastern outskirts of Coventry.

spots.name: 22 Bayley Lane
spots.summary: 22 Bayley Lane is a grade II* listed building and only remaining mediaeval timber framed building in the Cathedral Quarter area of Coventry, where there were at one time a great many.

spots.name: Hearsall Common
spots.summary: Hearsall Common is located in Earlsdon, Coventry in the West Midlands, central England.

spots.name: Mediaeval Stone Building, Coventry
spots.summary: The Medieval Stone Building is an unidentified medieval ruin on Much Park Street, Coventry, in the West Midlands of England. The ruin is a Grade II* listed building; it is believed to have been built in the late 13th or early 14th century and was uncovered by a German bomb during the Coventry Blitz.

spots.name: Blue Coat School
spots.summary: The Old Blue Coat School is a building in the city centre of Coventry, England. It was built in 1856 on the site of the Priory of St Mary, and is currently used by the Holy Trinity Church.

spots.name: St Osburg's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Osburg's Church also known as the Church of the Most Holy Sacrament and St Osburg is a Roman Catholic parish church in Coventry, West Midlands. It was built from 1843 to 1845 and was designed by Charles Hansom. It is situated in the city centre on the junction between Holyhead Road and the Coventry Ring Road.

spots.name: Whitefriars, Coventry

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The buildings known as Whitefriars are the surviving fragments of a Carmelite friary founded in 1342 in Coventry, England. It was initially home to a friary until the dissolution of the monasteries.

spots.name: Allesley Park
spots.summary: Allesley Park is a park in Coventry, West Midlands, England. It is also the name of the residential suburb adjacent to the park, which is approximately 2.5 miles (4 km) northwest of Coventry city centre, just east of the A45 Coventry bypass.

spots.name: Allesley Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Allesley Castle is a former motte and bailey castle in Allesley, Coventry. The mound has never been excavated. All that remains of the castle is a large mound - the motte - and a defensive ditch approximately 45 metres (148 ft) in diameter.

spots.name: Chamberlaine's Almshouses
spots.summary: The Nicholas Chamberlaine Almshouses are Grade II* listed almshouses in the town centre of Bedworth, Warwickshire, England. Dating from 1840, they remain in use for their original purpose.

spots.name: Vignoles Bridge
spots.summary: Vignoles Bridge is a footbridge over the River Sherbourne in Spon End, a western suburb of Coventry in central England. It stands just west of the inner ring road in the middle of a housing estate, to where it was relocated in 1969. It was built in 1835 and originally spanned the Oxford Canal.

spots.name: Spon Bridge
spots.summary: Spon Bridge is a bridge carrying Spon Street across the River Sherbourne in Coventry, central England.

spots.name: Coombe Country Park
spots.summary: Coombe Country Park is a country park located in Warwickshire, England. The park is only 4.5 miles east of Coventry city centre and is managed by Coventry City Council. The park has been developed from the grounds of an old Cistercian abbey, the buildings of which have now been converted into the Coombe Abbey hotel.

names.ja: クーム・カントリー・パーク

spots.name: St Francis of Assisi, Bedworth

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Roman Catholic Parish Church of Saint Francis of Assisi is located in Bedworth, Warwickshire, England. The parish is part of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Birmingham and a part of the Rugby Deanery. The current Parish Priest is Fr. Michael Gamble.

spots.name: Bayley Lane
spots.summary: Bayley Lane is a historic street in the centre of Coventry and is thought to follow the line of the outer ditch or bailey of the former Coventry Castle, founded by the Earls of Chester between 1088 and 1147.

spots.name: Nailcote Hall
spots.summary: Nailcote Hall is a 17th century country house hotel located near Berkswell, West Midlands, England.

spots.name: St Bartholomew's Church, Binley

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St Bartholomew is a church on Brinklow Road in Binley, in the City of Coventry in the West Midlands of England. The building is grade I listed, though churches in ecclesiastical use are exempt from listed building procedures.

photo.author: Carmen McLean-Ellmann, Oliver Ellmann (Wikipedia Takes Coventry participant)

spots.name: Coat of Arms Bridge
spots.summary: The Coat of Arms Bridge is a railway bridge in the Stivichall area of Coventry in the West Midlands of England. It carries the Coventry–Leamington line between Coventry and Leamington Spa and is located just south of Coventry railway station.

spots.name: Coventry University
spots.summary: Established in 1992 and located in buildings across the city centre, headquartered around University Square. Traditionally strong in engineering and design, the university's reputation has grown to one of the best modern universities in the country.

spots.name: Coventry Canal
spots.summary: Starts just outside the ring road, to the north of the city centre. After five miles it connects with the Oxford Canal at Hawkesbury Junction, then the Ashby-de-la-Zouch Canal at Marston Junction, just outside Bedworth. It next meets the Birmingham and Fazeley Canal at Fazeley Junction, near [[Tamworth (England)

spots.name: Snax in the City
spots.summary: A city centre greasy spoon café with big portions. Pleasantly staffed, they offer a wide choice of hot and cold meals for either eating-in or taking out. The value of the food is the strongest aspect; in respect of this, some of the food may appear distinctly average.

spots.name: Bombay Joe's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Highly rated amongst Coventrians, offering a range of Indian and Bangladeshi cuisine. Look beyond its location in the less prosperous part of Coventry and you will find a rich culinary experience. Their chairs are also rather comfortable.

spots.name: Zorbaz

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Excellent Greek restaurant, and the prices reflect this. Visit at the right time and you might hear a musician playing Greek songs and see the waiters treat you to some Greek dancing.

spots.name: Habibi

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Better Lebanese food will not be found in Coventry. The atmosphere and the staff are equally inviting. One downside is the service being a bit on the slow side.

spots.name: Turmeric Gold

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed

spots.summary: Stylishly-themed Indian restaurant within a medieval building. Waiting times for food may sometimes be long, but the quality of the food makes up for it.

spots.name: The Flying Standard

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Franchise of the ubiquitous Wetherspoons chain is set in a spectacular timbered building

spots.name: The Park Bistro
spots.summary: Locally-owned, offering a relaxed atmosphere and coffee and refreshments at low prices.
